subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In the reaction 2Mg + O2 -> 2MgO, the magnesium has been:
questions.explain: Magnesium gains oxygen and loses electrons, so it is oxidised.

questions.q: Some unreactive metals such as gold are found in the Earth as:
questions.explain: Very unreactive metals like gold are so unreactive they are found as the uncombined native metal.

questions.q: What is observed when a small piece of sodium is added to water?
options: It fizzes, moves on the surface and releases hydrogen
It turns the water bright blue
questions.explain: Sodium reacts vigorously with water, fizzing as it produces hydrogen gas and sodium hydroxide.

questions.q: Why is aluminium extracted by electrolysis rather than reduction with carbon?
options: Aluminium does not form an ore
Aluminium is more reactive than carbon
Aluminium is less reactive than carbon
questions.explain: Aluminium is more reactive than carbon, so carbon cannot reduce its oxide and electrolysis must be used.

questions.q: Calcium reacts with cold water to produce calcium hydroxide and which gas?
questions.explain: A metal reacting with water gives a metal hydroxide and hydrogen gas.

questions.q: Iron is extracted from its ore in the blast furnace by reduction with which substance?
questions.explain: Iron is less reactive than carbon, so carbon reduces iron oxide to iron in the blast furnace.

questions.q: Why are alloys such as steel usually harder than the pure metal?
options: The atoms are all identical and slide easily
Different sized atoms distort the layers so they cannot slide easily
questions.explain: Different sized atoms in an alloy distort the regular layers, making it harder for them to slide.

questions.q: Which list places the metals in order from most reactive to least reactive?
questions.explain: Going down the reactivity series the order is potassium, then magnesium, then zinc, then copper.

questions.q: Which mixture would NOT react, because no displacement is possible?
questions.explain: Copper is less reactive than zinc, so it cannot displace zinc from its solution.

questions.q: In a sacrificial protection system, the metal attached to iron must be:
questions.explain: A more reactive metal corrodes in preference to the iron, protecting it sacrificially.

questions.q: Why does oiling or greasing iron tools help prevent rusting?
options: It keeps out water and oxygen
It makes the iron more reactive
questions.explain: A barrier of oil keeps water and oxygen away from the iron surface.

questions.q: Which metal will displace copper from copper sulfate solution?
questions.explain: Iron is more reactive than copper, so it displaces copper from copper sulfate solution.

questions.q: Which metal could be used to extract iron from iron oxide by displacement?
questions.explain: Aluminium is more reactive than iron, so it can displace iron from iron oxide.

questions.q: Gold used in jewellery is often alloyed with copper mainly to:
options: Make it harder and more hard-wearing
questions.explain: Pure gold is soft, so it is alloyed with copper to make it harder.

questions.q: In the reactivity series, which of these metals is the most reactive?
questions.explain: Potassium is near the top of the reactivity series, far above iron, zinc and copper.

questions.q: A reactive metal can be extracted from its molten compound by electrolysis because:
options: Carbon is more reactive than the metal
The metal melts and floats off
Electricity decomposes the compound, depositing the metal
questions.explain: Electrolysis uses electricity to break down the compound, releasing the metal at the cathode.

questions.q: In terms of electrons, oxidation is best described as:
questions.explain: Using OILRIG, Oxidation Is Loss of electrons.

questions.q: In a displacement reaction, the more reactive metal:
questions.explain: The more reactive metal loses electrons to form ions, so it is oxidised.

questions.q: How does galvanising protect iron from rusting?
options: By adding carbon to the iron
By coating it with a layer of zinc
questions.explain: Galvanising coats iron with zinc, which acts as both a barrier and sacrificial protection.

questions.q: Which two substances are both needed for iron to rust?
questions.explain: Rusting of iron requires both water and oxygen to be present.

questions.q: Which gas is produced when magnesium reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid?
questions.explain: Reactive metals react with dilute acids to produce a salt and hydrogen gas.

questions.q: Which of these metals is the least reactive?
questions.explain: Gold is at the bottom of the reactivity series, making it the least reactive listed.
